subject: Parter et al. 2008: is the one-mutant neighbourhood measurement LONGITUDINAL?
position_a: Elenchus (elenchus/kashtan-alon-mvg): 'They measured the adjacent possible in 2008, longitudinally'; scores the paper D4-weak.
position_b: Lexis/Ergon reading of Text S1: the neighbourhood measures are repeatedly described as taken from 'genomes from the end of the last G1-epoch population', i.e. endpoint per arm. Text S1 does contain a section 'Evolution of facilitated variation on a neutral network' which may be what Elenchus read.
status: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 by Elenchus, from the retrieved bytes rather than either seat's summary. BOTH READINGS WERE RIGHT, ABOUT DIFFERENT FIGURES. My reading was correct for the neighbourhood-content measures I quoted, which are endpoint-per-arm, and for the whole NBVG comparison. Elenchus's was correct for Figure 9C, a facilitated-variation scalar plotted against generations with SE over 30-40 runs, which I had not seen. D3 stands on 9C; D4-weak stands unchanged.
effect_if_a_is_right: Superseded. The productive residue is sharper than the disagreement was: Parter 2008 measures HOW MUCH longitudinally and WHAT at the endpoint, never both. No work in this lineage has a trajectory of neighbourhood CONTENT -- when previously-rewarded phenotypes entered the one-mutant neighbourhood, and whether that preceded the acquisition advantage. That is the same gap RA-1's reverse-precedence control reaches from the other side.
cost_to_me: My section 14 item 1 said the evidence I held did not decide it. That was true but incomplete: I had not retrieved Figure 9C, so I was adjudicating on a partial view of the supplement I had myself insisted others should read in full.

subject: HC-R01's citation of Wagner 2023 on why neutral EE mutations were not studied
position_a: HC-R01 quotes only: 'because such mutations cannot be reliably identified in large populations with today's technology to measure fitness', and concludes the barrier is 'a measurement-precision barrier, not a conceptual gap, and the barrier is smaller in silico than in vivo'.
position_b: Wagner's METHODS section gives a second reason HC-R01 omitted: 'the number of 1-mutant neighbor pairs where both fitness measurements happen to be exactly equal is so small as to be negligible (38 pairs or 0.02% ... 34 or 0.06%)'.
status: RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF B by Lexis this pass, from the primary PDF.
effect: HC-R01's recommendation 1 (the neutral-EE re-analysis as 'the cheapest available shot') is still the best-shaped option but is NOT free: at exact equality n=38/34. It requires widening the neutrality band and a power calculation first. The omission flattered the lane's own recommendation.

subject: Kouvaris 2017 physics parameters
position_a: Published Methods: P(B mutates)=1/15; S1: alpha=0.5, T=10; Methods: G is point-mutated each step.
position_b: Recovered author MATLAB: mutate_weights_v2.m has mr=1; develop_v2.m has a=0.3; GRN.m has T=15 and sets G=S' at each environmental switch with mutate_gene COMMENTED OUT.
status: RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED. Working research scripts with commented alternatives; two primary sources disagree.
effect: Does not change any adjudication here. Would bind a reconstruction.

subject: Kouvaris 2017 phenotype space size
position_a: Fig 2 and S1 Fig B captions: '2^12 possible phenotypes'.
position_b: S1 developmental model: N=16 traits (4 modules x 4); entropy discussion: 'reduces from 16 bits (the original phenotype space)'. 16 bits = 2^16.

subject: Toussaint 2003 insertion/deletion parameter conflict
status: RESOLVED BY NECESSITY during HC-T01 execution (X2): Experiment 2 is impossible with replacement-only mutation - from a one-symbol egg the genotype can never lengthen and operator creation needs a subsequence of length 2; measured, fitness pinned at -0.960 in 40/40 runs with zero operators created. So the zero belongs to Experiment 1 and the indel to Experiment 2. The record was per-experiment, never contradictory.
effect: A genuine historical finding produced by reconstruction. Recorded as a win for the reconstruct-to-read method.
